# Existing Lesson Patterns — Research Findings

## HTML Structure Conventions

### Page Shell (generated by `tools/lib/page_template.py`)

Every lesson page follows this skeleton:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Lesson N: Title</title>
  <script src="../assets/typography-prefs.js"></script>       <!-- blocking prefs -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="../assets/style.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="../assets/glossary.css">       <!-- if glossary data exists -->
  <script type="importmap">{ ... Preact/HTM/Signals ... }</script>
</head>
<body>

<nav class="page-nav" aria-label="Breadcrumb">...</nav>
<h1>Title</h1>
<div class="lesson-meta">
  Lesson N · Domain · ~Xmin read<br>
  <strong>Win:</strong> One-sentence learning outcome
</div>
<div class="key-concept">
  <strong>After this lesson:</strong> Expanded outcome...
</div>

<!-- Body: h2 sections with content -->

<!-- Exercise (inside .next-steps div) -->
<!-- Code Files section (download links) -->
<!-- What's Next (inside .next-steps div) -->

<script type="application/json" id="glossary-data">{...}</script>
<script type="module" src="../assets/page-shell.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
```

### Key Structural Rules

1. **`data-theme="dark"`** on `<html>` — typography-prefs.js may override
2. **Breadcrumb nav**: `All Lessons › Domain Map › Current Page`
3. **lesson-meta div**: Lesson number, domain name, reading time, Win statement
4. **key-concept div**: Expanded "after this lesson" — what the learner can DO
5. **glossary-data script**: JSON island at bottom, before page-shell.js
6. **page-shell.js**: Single entry point for nav, glossary, typography, layout — always last script

### Import map

Preact + hooks + signals + signals-core + HTM — all vendored from `assets/vendor/`. Paths adjusted by depth (e.g., `../assets/vendor/` for depth=1).

---

## Template Generator (`page_template.py`)

### Architecture

- **Single source of truth** for all page HTML shells
- `_base_page()` — core function emitting DOCTYPE through `</html>`
- Page-type wrappers: `render_lesson_page`, `render_reference_page`, `render_quiz_page`, `render_map_page`, `render_index_page`, `render_resources_page`

### `render_lesson_page()` parameters

| Param | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `title` | str | Lesson title (used in h1 and breadcrumb) |
| `lesson_number` | int | Lesson N in the meta block |
| `domain` | str | Human-readable domain name |
| `domain_slug` | str | URL-safe domain (for map page link) |
| `lesson_id` | str | File stem (e.g., "0003-spatial-shader-anatomy") |
| `reading_time` | int | Minutes |
| `win` | str | One-sentence Win statement |
| `body_content` | str | Everything BELOW key-concept — h2 sections, exercises, code blocks |
| `glossary_data` | dict | Term→definition pairs for the glossary island |
| `key_concept` | str | "After this lesson:" text |
| `depth` | int | Directory depth for path prefix (default 1) |

### What the template generates vs what the caller provides

**Template generates:**
- `<head>` boilerplate (meta, prefs script, stylesheet, import map)
- Breadcrumb navigation
- `<h1>`, lesson-meta div, key-concept div
- Glossary JSON island
- page-shell.js script tag

**Caller provides:**
- `body_content` — ALL section content (h2s, paragraphs, SVGs, tables, exercises, code blocks, What's Next)

## Component Patterns (from real lessons)

### Key Concept Callout (`.key-concept`)

```html
<div class="key-concept">
  <strong>After this lesson:</strong> You can create and apply a spatial shader...
</div>
```

- One per lesson at the top (generated by template from `key_concept` param)
- Can also appear mid-lesson for critical rules (e.g., coordinate space rule in 0003)

### Note Callouts (`.note`)

```html
<div class="note">
<strong>Live editing:</strong> Godot recompiles shaders instantly...
</div>

<div class="note">
<strong>Critical:</strong> light() is called multiple times...
</div>
```

- Used for gotchas, warnings, FYI info
- Always has a `<strong>` label identifying the type

### Exercises (`.next-steps` > Check Your Understanding)

```html
<div class="next-steps">
  <h3>Check Your Understanding</h3>
  <p><strong>Exercise:</strong> scenario description...</p>
  <details>
    <summary>Hint</summary>
    <p>...</p>
  </details>
  <details>
    <summary>Answer</summary>
    <p>explanation...</p>
    <pre>...</pre>  <!-- optional code in answer -->
  </details>
</div>
```

- Tests the lesson's Win statement (not gotchas)
- Pattern: "A colleague did X. What's wrong and why?" (misconception probing)
- Uses `<details>` for progressive reveal (hint then answer)

### Code Blocks

```html
<pre data-file="toon_test.gdshader"><code>...</code></pre>
<pre data-file="toon_smoothstep.gdshader" data-mode="diff"><code>...</code></pre>
<pre data-mode="fragment"><code>...</code></pre>
```

- `data-file` — target filename (extractable, must have downloadable counterpart)
- `data-mode` — `complete` (default), `diff` (patch), `fragment` (illustration only)
- Diff blocks use `<span style="color:var(--success)">+added</span>` / `<span style="color:var(--error)">-removed</span>`

### Code Files Section

```html
<h2>Code Files</h2>
<p>Download the final-state shader from this lesson:</p>
<ul>
  <li><a href="../reference/code/spatial-shader-anatomy/toon_test.gdshader" download><code>toon_test.gdshader</code></a> — description</li>
</ul>
```

- Required when lesson has `data-file` blocks
- Links to `reference/code/{lesson-slug}/`

### What's Next (`.next-steps`)

```html
<div class="next-steps">
  <h3>What's Next</h3>
  <p><strong>Lesson N:</strong> <a href="...">Title</a> — preview of next lesson</p>
  <p><strong>Reference:</strong> <a href="...">cheat sheet link</a></p>
</div>
```

### SVG Diagrams (inline)

- Always: `role="img"`, `aria-labelledby`, `<title>` as first child
- Always: `viewBox` only (no fixed width/height), `style="max-width:100%; height:auto;"`
- Colors: `var(--svg-primary)`, `var(--svg-success)`, `var(--svg-warning)`, `var(--svg-neutral)`, etc.
- Labels ON the diagram (spatial contiguity)

### Glossary Terms (inline)

```html
<span class="term" data-term="node">nodes</span>
```

- Links to the glossary-data JSON island
- page-shell.js adds tooltip behavior

### Citations

```html
<a href="URL" class="citation">[Source Name]</a>
```

## Lightweight vs Substantial Lessons (Observed Differences)

### Lesson 0001 (Nodes & Scenes) — Foundational/Orientation

- **~10 min read**
- **No code files section** (no runnable code, purely conceptual)
- **No `data-file` blocks** (code examples are illustrative only)
- **Content is conceptual**: explains architecture, mental models, rules
- **Tables used heavily**: node types, lifecycle callbacks
- **SVG diagrams**: show structure (tree relationships), not pipelines
- **Exercise**: design exercise ("what nodes would you use?"), not debug exercise
- **Win**: "explain the architecture" — understanding, not implementation

### Lesson 0003 (Spatial Shader Anatomy) — Orientation for a Track

- **~10 min read** (matches lightweight)
- **HAS code files section** (produces a runnable shader)
- **HAS `data-file` blocks** (toon_test.gdshader)
- **Setup-first structure**: "get it running, then understand what you built"
- **Exercise**: debug exercise (identify missing fragment() — misconception probing)
- **Win**: "create a shader, assign it, explain the three functions" — both do AND understand
- **References section**: links to official docs AND community tutorials

### Lesson 0004 (Toon Banding) — Substantial

- **~12 min read**
- **Multiple `data-file` blocks** (several shader variants)
- **Problem→Solution arc**: "two bands isn't enough → here are three approaches"
- **Diff-mode code blocks**: shows modifications to existing shader
- **SVG diagrams**: compare visual results (2-band vs 4-band)
- **Builds on previous lesson**: "start from the previous shader"
- **Decision callouts**: when to use which approach

### Key Distinctions

| Aspect | Lightweight/Orientation | Substantial |
|--------|------------------------|-------------|
| Reading time | ~10 min | 10-15 min |
| Code blocks | Illustrative or single runnable file | Multiple files, diff progression |
| Exercise type | Design/explain | Debug/apply |
| Structure | Concept → examples → rules | Problem → approaches → trade-offs |
| Code Files section | Maybe (if any code is runnable) | Always (multiple files) |
| References | Official docs | Docs + community + prior art table |
| Win verb | "explain", "understand" | "implement", "choose between" |

### The 0003 Pattern (Orientation-that-produces-code)

Lesson 0003 is the closest analog to what an "orientation" lesson in a new track looks like. It:
1. Gets something running FIRST (setup section)
2. Then explains what was just built
3. Introduces vocabulary/concepts needed for subsequent lessons
4. Produces a single runnable artifact (the minimal shader)
5. Exercise tests understanding of the pipeline concept, not a gotcha
6. Explicitly sets up the next lesson ("we'll add shadow coloring next")

This is the pattern for a prerequisite lesson that enables a track — substantial enough to produce runnable code, but focused on "what IS this" rather than "which approach to choose."
